w: In the evening assembly, volunteers of the Children's Wing presented a program 'Thaiye Yogi Jeva'. The program presentation symbolically showed how the moon and sun narrated the efforts of Pramukh Swami Maharaj in inspiring and pleasing the devotees regardless of physical discomforts, his devotion to God and his saintliness. The one-hour presentation included a traditional dance and prayers by the volunteers.

Morning & Evening Programs During the evening cultural assembly, all those present realised the greatness of Shastriji Maharaj through a variety of presentations that described his accomplishments despite the obstacles he faced to spread the Akshar Purushottam upasana. Swamishri concluded the assembly with blessings, during which he narrated several incidents from Shastriji Maharaj's life, such as, the murti-pratishtha of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj in Vadhwan, and the construction of five spectacular mandirs. He also emphasised the importance of the Akshar Purushottam upasana.
A youth came for darshan. He said, "I keep worrying, so I cannot even sleep."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Worry will certainly keep one awake, because that is how the mind is. So pray to God, leave it to God without worrying about the result, and make your effort while remembering God."

Abhayswarup Swami phoned from Mumbai. A few days earlier he had had to be admitted to hospital because of malaria, and Pramukh Swami Maharaj had received this news. Although Abhayswarup Swami had phoned about some other work, Swamishri immediately said, "First tell me about yourself. Has your fever come down?"
Abhayswarup Swami said, "It came down on Sunday. We have come back to the mandir."
Swamishri said, "Take care. There is a lot of fever going around, so take care."

The well known youth volunteer Aku Patel phoned from London. When the sadhus from London came to India for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan, Swamishri had naturally remembered Aku and asked, "How is his business going?" When Aku came to know of this, he gratefully phoned Swamishri himself and said, "You take such great care of us. You remembered me in front of the sadhus, so I have made this call. By your grace the business is going well. You have graciously arranged everything. Please bless us that we engage in seva with body, mind and wealth."

Though Abhayswarup Swami had phoned about some other work, Swamishri immediately said, "First tell me about yourself. Has your fever gone down?"
Abhayswarup Swami said, "It has been down since Sunday. We have come back to the mandir."
Swamishri said, "Take care. Fever is going around, so take care."

Aku Patel, a well known youth volunteer, phoned from London. When the sants from London came to India for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's darshan, Swamishri had casually remembered Aku and asked how his business was going. When Aku came to know of this, out of gratitude he himself phoned Swamishri and said, "You take such care of us. You remembered me before the sants, that is why I have phoned. By your grace the business is going well. In your compassion you have arranged everything. Please bless us so that we engage in seva with body, mind and wealth."

ds.t: What he sees with eyes closed
w: Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the Children's Day assembly. Speaking about manasi (mental worship), a child said, "Swami! When we close our eyes, we see darkness. What do you see when you close your eyes? Please write it for us."
An iPad was held in front of Swamishri. Swamishri wrote, "Yogi Bapa," and he even said, "I see Yogi Bapa."

Remembering this incident, after the midday meal was over, the attendant sadhu asked Swamishri the secret of why he had actually closed his eyes to write the answer to the child's question. Swamishri said very simply, "They had said, write what you see when you close your eyes."
Everyone laughed.
Swamishri laughed and said, "One must follow commands."
The sadhus said, "You followed the children's command."
Swamishri said meaningfully, "Then they will follow ours."
What a great principle!
Munichintandas Swami asked, "After you closed your eyes, did you see Yogi Bapa?"
Swamishri said joyfully, "I see him twenty four hours a day."
Yogiji Maharaj had said, "I have constant darshan of Bhagwan." The same feeling came through in Swamishri's answer.
Today, during Mahant Swami Maharaj's walk, a reading from Yogi Vani began, along with Swamishri's wonderful commentary.

From the book was read: "Fight with the mind, saying, 'I will smash you to pieces,' but do not be troubled. What is left for us now? We have met Shriji Maharaj in person, so do not be troubled and get going with faith. What weight do faults have? They will go away like this."
Swamishri too snapped his fingers and said, "They will go away like this."
The sadhus said, "What does 'they will go away like this' mean?"
Showing the way, Swamishri said, "We have to keep a sense of alertness. If a snake has got into our room, we do not know when it will bite, so we have to be careful."

Then he said, "Our attainment is as big as Mount Meru and our faults are a clod of earth. If one thinks of the attainment, the faults and everything go away. Nothing remains. This has also been said in Gadhada II 13."

It was read further: "What is greatness? Getting a cushioned seat, getting a raised platform? Greatness is keeping peace in the heart. If the virtues of the great sadhu have come into you, there will be peace in the heart."
Swamishri said, "Even if he is sitting in a corner and no one asks after him, there is peace. Peace within. Another may be sitting on 14 mattresses spread out and still have no peace."
The reader read on: "What is the greatest seva? To know the great sadhu as free of faults."
Swamishri said, "This is the greatest seva. We think that lifting a load of 10 maunds is seva, but even if one does not move an inch, this way is the greatest seva..."
Next came: "One should like the actions of Bhagwan and the great sadhu; only then do their virtues come, and then one does as they say."
Swamishri said, "It is not just tolerating the actions of the great sadhu; one should like whatever action the great sadhu does. There should be a sense of divinity; then virtues come."
It was read further: "To see divinity and faultlessness in the guru is the worship of the guru."

Swamishri said, "This is the true thing. If one sees him as faultless, dharma and everything come with it." Then, with a gesture, he said, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj never went to do the pujan of Yogi Bapa. He was always busy in seva. But he saw him as faultless!" Then he said, "Do not deliberately create such a thing (of not going to do pujan); if you get the chance, take the benefit."

The book was read further. In it came: "Of the four kinds of medicinal herbs, sanjivani (the life restoring herb) is special. It is devotion with the understanding that the great sadhu is faultless. To become gunatit, do not see faults in anyone. We have been sent from Akshardham to offer devotion with this understanding of faultlessness."
Swamishri asked, "What have we been sent for?"
The sadhus said, "To offer devotion with the understanding of faultlessness."
Swamishri said, "Not to rush about."
It was read further: "What should one do?"
Before Yogi Bapa's answer could be read, Swamishri burst out, "Rush about..." The sadhus laughed.
Then Yogi Bapa's sentence was read: "Associate with the sadhu in thought, deed and word."
It was read further: "What should one know?"
Here too Swamishri blew the first puff, saying, "About the whole world!" Again there was laughter.
Then Yogi Bapa's sentence was read: "The discernment between the inert and the conscious."
In this way, Swamishri gives teachings even through humour.

The reader read on: "Do not gossip about one another. The nature of telling one person's talk to another and another's talk to someone else leaves a flaw on the path of sadhuhood. So one who wants moksha should give up that nature."

Swamishri said, "Even if the talk is true, it is called gossip. For example, even if someone really is always sleeping or always eating, it should not be said. And if nothing like that has happened and one says it, that is great gossip."
Finally it was read: "Swami used to say to Jaga Bhakta: do not let others' actions, others' forms and others' faults into your soul."
Swamishri said, "You will die."
After every sentence, Swamishri spoke beautiful words of inspiration.
